thread: The flour supply chain: the young man with the cart, the ANDORHAL sacking, and the grain road

evidence.clue: Joss bought grain from the valley farms for twenty years; three months ago a young man with a cart came from the west road with barley and flour cheaper by two coppers on the measure; four loads since, the last a fortnight ago. The bakehouse takes all its flour from the granary; so do most houses on the near side of the brook and the top farm since harvest.

The man: young, civil, brown or fair hair, a good horse; paid in good coin; bought the keeper a jug at the alehouse; asked after his wife's leg. Joss 'would know him again'. Sylvanas and Jaina: he is the same man as Millhaven's 'cheaper than Mister Hollis'.
The loft held most of the last load: new pale sacks stencilled with a wheat sheaf in a ring and the word ANDORHAL. Sylvanas cut a square of the sacking before it burned and carries it in her coat.
Brask: Andorhal is the big granaries, south and west, past the ford, three days by cart; 'Everything in the south goes through Andorhal, one way or another. My barley goes through Andorhal.'

Jaina: 'Then that's where his cart came from. Or where he wanted us to think it came from.' Sylvanas: 'Either way, it's the road he drove.' The party turns onto the grain road at the end of the chapter; the staff leans toward the ruts.
Joss sent a cart with flour that morning to the ford for the Hallams and the alehouse; Dickon turned it round; the alehouse had taken two sacks; Brask burns the lot.

Chapter 5, Corley's depot: the out-book lists 'own cart' short-rate loads (two coppers under, twelve sacks) from midsummer; counts by road before the last month / since: north 9/3, west 7/4, south 11/6, east 1/9; 31 places. 'And.' in the margin of nearly every line (loads come in from Andorhal). Carters' names are never written. Millhaven's first short-rate load was at midsummer.

Chapter 5, the table: 47 places, 19 in more than one book (Corley's, miller, hamlet shop, Wick, second depot). Second depot clerk: short-rate loads are booked in from the big river depot first; 'Everything on this side of the river goes over the overseer's scale.'

Chapter 5, river depot ash: 53 readable waybill halves (plus 9 with the destination burned) each with Andorhal at one end (From Andorhal / Andorhal stores / Recd. And. / To Andorhal, for breaking); 'Barov' on 31 of them; the sacking ANDORHAL laid at the narrow end of the fan.
Chapter 5, Jaina's marks cluster on the south road and the lanes off it; getting older the further south; a new thin layer on the old; the King's road is clean; the east road is only starting.
Chapter 5: Cyndia finds army-wagon tracks on the south road (iron tyres, King's post-horse shoe); Sylvanas pins Strahnbrad at the south road's end.

Chapter 6: Jaina lays the chain before Arthas: flour carried by wagons through mills into bread, the depot slips from the stove, Andorhal at one end of every slip, every road she has read heavy south of the Pass runs there, 'this one worst of all, old under new'; she asks for men to shut the Andorhal granaries. He does not. A village south of Millhaven would have gone the same way 'if we hadn't burned every sack of flour in it in one night.'

Chapter 6: below Strahnbrad the south road fills with grain carts coming in from farm lanes and empty carts leaving; each farm lane joining adds 'a fresh thread of lateness' to the drag. Andorhal on first sight is a working granary city: a granary quarter of tall square timber buildings on stone feet with hoist beams, grain dust gold in the low sun, wagons waiting in lines to enter, ovens baking.

Chapter 6: the tally-man says authority over the granaries is split three ways (factors, the corn guild, the town) and that Captain Havel of the militia 'knows the granary district better than anybody. Better than the factors do, and they'd sooner not hear it.'

Chapter 7: the ANDORHAL stencil is real and in use in the city: open sacks on Kett's loft floor carry the sheaf-in-a-ring with lettering under it; Sylvanas touches the square of sacking cut from Brask's loft ('lettering under it that she knew').

Chapter 7: Fenner's and the Exchange changed suppliers in the same week at high summer (new carters, new loaders, a factor nobody at the Exchange has shaken hands with); Garside's took a little at Lammas and stopped ('the price was too good'); Kett's and the old malt-house at the weir end took the same factor's grain the same month. The same factor's grain now rides out on copied yard marks (forty-one bills Corin will swear to, south, weir and east roads).
Chapter 7: Kett's bills are all for the first carts out; seven loaded carts leave down the lane at night. The south road is where Fenner's copied mark mostly points.

readerKnows_chapter7: The Andorhal stencil is real and sewn shut at Kett's; the contaminated grain is dispatched under other yards' copied marks; the 'young man with the cart' and the factor remain faceless.
povCharacterKnows_chapter7: Sylvanas and Jaina: the grain is treated at packaging by hand in Andorhal and sent out on copied marks; the new factor is a name on contracts. They do not know who the factor is.
readerKnows_chapter6: Andorhal is alive and busy and the grain still flows through it; the party will approach through the market gate and ask for Havel.
povCharacterKnows_chapter6: Jaina: whoever keeps the spread running is inside Andorhal and knows which wagon goes to which yard and keeps the books. Sylvanas: the same, plus a wrong note in the farewell.
readerKnows_chapter5: The grain trade is a regional network with Andorhal at one end of every readable slip, short-rate loads since midsummer, a lord's seal (Barov) on the paper, a depot overseer who lied and burned the books, and the south road is worst by Jaina's read. The cart man is one of many carriers.
povCharacterKnows_chapter5: Sylvanas: not one man but somebody 'with yards and books and boys'; Andorhal is the hub; Barov is a connection, not a verdict; she cannot verify the south-road read. The stencil-as-decoy question is moved aside: Andorhal is the nexus, but where it goes in is unresolved.
readerKnows: A cheap flour from a stenciled Andorhal sack is the carrier; it came by a young man's cart from the west road; the party is following it to Andorhal.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina: suspects the stencil may be a decoy. Sylvanas: it is the only road there is. Neither has a name or face for the seller.
notes: Next chapter starts on the grain road southwest (plan: Chapter 5). The stencil may be a false trail. The old carter of Ch3 asked about a young grain man 'coming down from your way', yet this seller came from the west: no link stated. Do not resolve the Andorhal connection or give the seller a face yet.
